subject: Q3 consumption audit + stair-step expansion proposal
content:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@finwave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 consumption audit + stair-step expansion proposal

Asha —

Thanks again for the time last week. We completed a short consumption audit for FinWave (attached) and wanted to propose a stair-step commit that matches your burst patterns while keeping unit economics favorable. Quick summary:

- Current run-rate: ~1.6B tokens / month (Q2 avg).
- Peak-day bursts up to 3.4B tokens (model mix: text-gen-large + chat-embedding).
- Observed tail latency at peak: 180–220ms 95p on current Hosted tier; Dedicated would reduce that to ~90–110ms given your sequence profile.

Proposal (high level):
1) 12-month term with quarterly step-ups: start at 2B tokens/mo commitment for Q3, step to 3B Q4, 4B Q1 2028.
2) Unit price discounts applied at each step (5% / 8% / 12%) and a one-time onboarding credit.
3) SLA amendment for latency targets + predefined fallback model plan during maintenance windows.

Attached: Q2_FinWave_usage_report.csv (token breakdown), ROI_snapshot_FinWave_Q2.pdf, and a draft SLA_stairstep_amendment_draft.pdf with redlines.

If you want, we can run a short canary on Dedicated to show latency improvements before committing the Q4 increase. Can Marissa coordinate a 45-minute walkthrough next week?

Thanks,
Vivek
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---

From: Asha Patel <asha@finwave.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@finwave.ai>, procurement@finwave.ai, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 consumption audit + stair-step expansion proposal

Thanks Vivek — this is helpful. A few quick questions from our side:

1) On pricing: can you show a modeled total cost of ownership (TCO) vs our current pay-as-you-go for the next 12 months at the proposed steps? We need line items by model family and quantization tier.
2) Security/compliance: does the SLA draft include retention and audit-log language compatible with our data residency needs? Our security team will need that explicitly called out.
3) Procurement: is there flexibility on the start date of the term if we want the first step billed pro-rata?

Marissa — can you share the raw token-level CSV and a short ROI summary for the execs? Prefer a 1‑page executive slide.

Asha
VP Product
FinWave.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@finwave.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 consumption audit + stair-step expansion proposal

Hey Asha — attaching the raw CSV and a one-page ROI snapshot per your ask. Notes below:

- The CSV (Q2_FinWave_usage_report.csv) includes token-level cohorting by route, peak-hour buckets, and model family tags.
- ROI_snapshot_FinWave_Q2.pdf contains a 12-month TCO comparison (payg vs stair-step) with conservative latency benefit monetization: we model a 3–5% uplift in user engagement from lower tail latency in web flows.
- On retention/audit: SLA draft includes references to retention windows and audit log export APIs; Security wanted HSM/KMS language — Ben can confirm technical controls.

Proposed next steps:
- 45-minute technical canary runweek (Ben to scope): dedicated instance with mirrored traffic for 72h.
- Finance + Procurement sync to agree on prorated start date.
- Finalize SLA redlines and circulate for legal.

I'll set a Doodle for next Tue/Wed and include a short agenda.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q2_FinWave_usage_report.csv, ROI_snapshot_FinWave_Q2.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 01 Aug 2027 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 consumption audit + stair-step expansion proposal

Asha / Samir —

Quick tech notes ahead of the canary:
- We recommend mirroring the routes that account for 85% of your token spend (see CSV routing column).
- For the Dedicated mirror, please allow KV cache warm-up for 6–8 hours to see representative latency improvements.
- If you use embeddings at high cardinality, we suggest enabling prefix caching on the search route to cut token rates by ~12%.

I'll prepare a short runbook and an infra estimate (GPU-hours) for the 72h mirror and share by EOD tomorrow. If procurement wants the prorated start, that's straightforward — we can set effective_date on the amendment and prorate the first invoice.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SLA_stairstep_amendment_draft.pdf
